evidence_items.explanation: Block explicitly connected its workforce reduction to AI tools and reported increased production code per engineer. This challenges the categorical wording, but management's account does not independently measure how much human work AI actually replaced.

The author-hosted account reports randomized experiments involving 4,867 developers and increased completed tasks. This is substantial counterevidence to a general dismissal of productivity research, but it concerns earlier experiments and professional developers.

METR reported suggestive speedups but warned that selection effects made the new experiment unreliable for estimating current productivity. It neither establishes a general speedup nor supports a categorical absence of gains.

unresolved_gaps: The retrieved workforce records do not independently establish the extent of actual AI substitution.
No qualifying comparison of completed software delivery by non-technical users was found.
Earlier controlled productivity findings materially challenge the wording but fall outside the selected observation period.
The author-hosted study gives only a publication month; available_at uses that month's final day as a conservative availability bound.
